mechanism_narrative: Positive momentum in RETAIL_REC over the past four weeks (from -20.1 to -13.3) reflects adaptive shopping behavior that persists, causing the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC to exceed the prior 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -20.1 to -13.3 over the four weeks ending 2020-12-15
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the observed upward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility improves past -48 percent change from baseline, increased commuting and foot traffic lift discretionary retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -48 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -53.6 to -46.3 over the four weeks ending 2020-12-15
failure_condition: After TRANSIT exceeds -48, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the prior 14-day mean in a majority of such weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicate a broad return to out-of-home routines; this combined activity raises retail footfall, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -21.3 to -19.1 and TRANSIT rose from -53.6 to -46.3
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES > -20 and TRANSIT > -50 simultaneously, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A declining RESIDENTIAL mobility trend (from 8.1 to 5.1 percent above baseline) shows people spending less time at home, which increases out-of-home retail activity and lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 8.1 to 5.1 over the four weeks ending 2020-12-15
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility rises above zero percent change from baseline, households shift spending toward essentials and away from discretionary retail, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.0 to 0.7 over the four weeks ending 2020-12-15
failure_condition: When GROCERY_PHARM > 0, the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior 7-day mean in a majority of instances.

mechanism_narrative: The December holiday shopping season mechanically boosts retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the next four weeks independently of mobility restrictions.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-12-15 falls within the December holiday shopping period
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is less than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the holiday season being active.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening restrictions regime, falling TRANSIT and rising RESIDENTIAL signal reduced out-of-home activity, which suppresses retail visits and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: Under tightening restrictions (TRANSIT < -50 or RESIDENTIAL > 6), the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous jump in PARKS and TRANSIT mobility indicates broader geographic movement and outdoor activity that spills over into retail visits, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -21.9 to -10.9 and TRANSIT rose from -53.6 to -46.3
failure_condition: When PARKS > -15 and TRANSIT > -48 simultaneously, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.
